original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: On the one-array native interface, decide whether a set of the 56 PR1825 matched planes whose joint pairing has rank at most 2 can realize its strict identity for complete-plane copy mass strictly below 4 per plane.
scope_change_reason: Merged PR2203 prices the 56 blocks independently at copy mass 224 and leaves shared fractional totals open. The scoped fact is the quotient-collision restitution: on every form-rank-2 pair and triple, every legal one-array support still pays at least 2, so the identity costs at least 4 per plane. Cross-rank-1 supports and mixed orthogonal/non-orthogonal totals are left open, including the checked 24-plane conflict clique.
bottleneck_link: The two-unpaid-coordinate moment at copy mass 224 is 293/292. A discount below 4 per plane on a form-rank-2 collision would be the sharing that one collapsed total appears to offer. Restitution says that collision still pays 4 per plane.
stop_rule: Stop when every form-rank-2 set of the fixed 56 planes is shown to force complete-plane copy mass at least 4 per plane, or when an explicit factorization under that rate is found. Do not infer a new kappa.
evidence: verify.py rebuilds the 56 Gram-I2 planes from the pinned labels and matching, checks that the only form-rank-2 sets are 144 pairs and 8 triples, checks that every nonempty support inside those sets has pairing rank at least 2, and checks the identity-rank restitution 2*(2|S|)=4|S|. independent.py repeats the geometry without importing verify.py. Eight negative controls reject a corrupted certificate, duplicate JSON keys, a false orthogonal pair, and an undercounted triple bound.
author: Wentao Li <wentaol4@illinois.edu>
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for the collision-restitution argument, the verifier, and the independent checks.

open_questions.question: Can a one-total factorization that uses a cross-rank-1 support, or a total containing both an orthogonal plane pair and a non-orthogonal plane pair, make the global complete-plane copy mass strictly smaller than 224?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Form-rank-2 restitution already charges 4 per plane on every colliding pair and triple. A global mass below 224 has to use a support this package does not price, such as one of the 879 cross-rank-1 pairs or the checked 24-plane clique that contains 173 of them.
open_questions.first_step: Exhibit one such support, its pairing rank, and a signed cancellation of every forbidden cross, then price the induced complement.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such identity with complete-plane mass below 4 per plane of its support is known, and this package does not claim that none exists.
